statement_name: The Nashville Statement on Biblical Sexuality
release_event: Released by CBMW at the ERLC National Conference, Nashville TN, August 25, 2017; public announcement August 29, 2017
publisher: Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood (CBMW)
fetch_methodology: Two CBMW PDFs were downloaded: (a) the 8-page initial signatories list with role/institution attribution for ~152 founders (cbmw.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/The_Nashville_Statement_Initial_Signatories_List.pdf) and (b) the 145-page consolidated petition signers list dated 2025-07-22 (cbmw.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/CBMW-Nashville-Statement-Signers-07-22-25.pdf), which contains ~23,747 raw lines / ~22,763 unique name strings. Initial signers are richly attributed; petition entries are bare names only (no role/church/year on CBMW's public list). Notable additional signers (William Lane Craig, Ken Ham, Kees van der Staaij, Erwin Lutzer, Tom Pennington, Harry Reeder, Andy Davis, Mark Vroegop, Stephen Nichols, Everett Piper, David Bennett, etc.) confirmed via Wikipedia and CBMW petition-wall search. Cross-referenced against Dallas Statement (~13K) and the four soft-progressive PCA / Revoice lists.

with_dallas_statement_2018.note: Dallas Statement was 2018; many Nashville signers also signed Dallas. Strict name-string overlap between Dallas full list (~13K) and Nashville petition wall (~23K) is 1,709. Initial-signer overlap is heavier — most Dallas authors (MacArthur, Ascol, Mohler-adjacent) also Nashville initial.
with_dallas_statement_2018.caveat: Common-name collisions (John Smith, etc.) inflate this number; treat as upper bound.

with_warhurst_2020_pca.note: Warhurst signers oppose AMR/Revoice in PCA. Nashville initial-signer overlap = 0. Petition wall has 12 name-string matches (mostly common-name collisions: James Miller, Chris Smith, Greg Ward).

with_amr_pca_2026.note: AMR is the soft-progressive Kellerite PCA list. Zero overlap with Nashville (initial OR petition).

with_pca_letter_of_lament_2025.note: Letter of Lament (2025) is post-Greg-Johnson PCA progressive lament. Two name-string collisions in petition wall (Owen Lee, Howard Brown), almost certainly different people given the demographic gap.

with_revoice_speakers_endorsers.note: CONTESTED MIDDLE — two Nashville INITIAL signers also appear on Revoice list: (1) Sam Allberry (gay-celibate Anglican apologist; spoke at Revoice 1, has since distanced from Revoice trajectory but still represents Side B); (2) Karen Swallow Prior (signed Nashville while at Liberty; has been a notable Nashville-and-Revoice-adjacent voice and was sympathetic to early Revoice). David Bennett (Side B Anglican, A War of Loves author) appears on petition wall and Revoice — also contested middle.

publicly_distanced_or_repented.name: David French
publicly_distanced_or_repented.note: Initial Nashville signer (2017) as National Review writer. Publicly shifted in November 2022, supporting Respect for Marriage Act and arguing for civil same-sex marriage recognition in pluralist society. Has not formally retracted Nashville signature but is widely seen as having moved on the cultural-engagement question.

publicly_distanced_or_repented.name: James MacDonald
publicly_distanced_or_repented.note: Removed from Harvest Bible Chapel pulpit February 2019 over governance/abuse-of-power scandal — disqualified, though not over Nashville positions per se.

publicly_distanced_or_repented.name: Paige Patterson
publicly_distanced_or_repented.note: Fired by SWBTS May 2018 over mishandling of sexual abuse allegations. Removed from leadership but not formally distanced from Nashville positions.

publicly_distanced_or_repented.name: C. J. Mahaney
publicly_distanced_or_repented.note: Sovereign Grace Ministries underwent abuse lawsuit / ecclesial-discipline controversy 2011-2013; Mahaney left SGM 2013 and re-launched at Sovereign Grace Church Louisville. Signed Nashville from that platform; some have questioned the appropriateness given prior controversies.

publicly_distanced_or_repented.name: Joshua Harris (NOT a signer — explicitly declined and later renounced faith)
publicly_distanced_or_repented.note: Often confused. Harris did not sign Nashville. He renounced his book "I Kissed Dating Goodbye" 2018 and announced deconversion July 2019. Mentioned here only to forestall confusion.

publicly_named_non_signers_for_clarity.name: Tim Keller
publicly_named_non_signers_for_clarity.note: Despite the brief's working assumption, Tim Keller did NOT sign the Nashville Statement (2017). Keller's signature is one of the conspicuous absences — he was alive and active in 2017 but declined. This is the basis of the 'Kellerite vs Nashville' framing in subsequent PCA / TGC discourse. Keller did not sign Dallas Statement either.

publicly_named_non_signers_for_clarity.name: Russell Moore
publicly_named_non_signers_for_clarity.note: Did sign Nashville as initial signer (2017). Moore left the SBC in 2021 over unrelated abuse / Trump-era controversies. He has not formally distanced from Nashville — but his post-2021 cultural engagement has softened tone. The brief's note that 'Moore later distanced from some statement positions' is overstated; he has not retracted.

notes: Methodology and caveats: (1) The 152 'initial signatories' captured here are the founding cohort published by CBMW August 2017, with full role/institution attribution. (2) The remaining ~22,600 entries are from CBMW's open online petition wall (most recent snapshot 2025-07-22), which is unverified and unmoderated — entries are bare names with no titles, institutions, or signing dates. Year_signed is null for petition entries because the petition wall does not record dates. (3) Common-name collisions are inevitable in a 22K-name list; cross-reference matches against other lists should be treated as candidate overlaps requiring human verification, not confirmed identity matches. (4) The Nashville Statement is broader and earlier than the Dallas Statement (2018): Dallas was John MacArthur's narrower 'Statement on Social Justice & the Gospel' in response to perceived TGC/Big-Eva drift. Many Nashville signers (Mohler, Carson, Akin, Greear) did NOT sign Dallas. Conversely most Dallas signers had already signed Nashville. (5) Tim Keller did NOT sign Nashville — this is a key historical fact and is the origin of the 'Kellerite' vs Nashville-orthodox framing in subsequent PCA discourse. (6) Karen Swallow Prior and Sam Allberry are the most notable contested-middle figures: both initial Nashville signers AND on the Revoice speaker/endorser list. (7) David French publicly shifted on civil same-sex marriage in November 2022 but has not formally retracted his Nashville signature. (8) James MacDonald, Paige Patterson, C. J. Mahaney all faced subsequent controversies unrelated (or partially related) to Nashville positions. (9) For the MOOP church directory, signing Nashville is a strong GREEN signal on biblical-sexuality orthodoxy as of 2017, but it does NOT certify orthodoxy on every other front — several initial signers were later disqualified from ministry for governance / character / other-doctrine issues.
